answer: Sequential VDF registration requires each agent to hash its public key with an epoch beacon, compute a strict squaring chain on one execution thread, and submit a short proof before a tight window closes. Because time-sharing vCPUs or splitting steps across a GPU orchard fails the deadline, attackers incur dedicated, unshared fast-core time and power per identity. Still, an operator using custom ASICs or scavenging spot compute like a raven can mint multiple identities.
